items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Fats was a big fan of Roy Eldridge and also Howard McGee and yet, even at that time, Fats had his own unique way of improvising on trumpet.

ctx.x: Yeah, I think it was Clarence Love. I think it was LaVon Kemp, I think Clarence Love was the next situation, and then Snookum Russell. The Snookum Russell thing was important. It was a very good band. They traveled a lot. It was in the Snookum Russell band that I met Fats Navarro, who was certainly to become one of the giants of jazz in later years. Fats Navarro and I were road buddies. We rode side by side. We’d sit side by side on the bus. We roomed together. We were true buddy- buddy buddies. Fats was a big…
situation was Benny Carter, I believe.
